statement: For f in C(0, 2pi), the numbers (f, phi_k) obtained by integrating f against the orthonormal trigonometric functions; they are the coefficients in the projection f_n of f on S.
quotes: The numbers $(f, \varphi_k)$ are called Fourier coefficients of $f$ .

statement: An element in V is said to be orthogonal to a subset S if it is orthogonal to every element of S.
quotes: An element in V is said to be orthogonal to S if it is orthogonal to every element of S.

statement: The distance between two elements x and y of a Euclidean space is defined to be the norm of x - y.
quotes: The distance between two elements x and y is defined to be the norm

statement: If S is a subspace of a Euclidean space, the set S-perp of all elements orthogonal to S is called the orthogonal complement of S.
quotes: In case S is a subspace, then $S^{\perp}$ is called the orthogonal complement of S.

statement: Given a finite-dimensional subspace S of a Euclidean space V and an element x in V, the problem is to determine an element in S whose distance from x is as small as possible.
quotes: Given an element x in V, to determine an element in S whose distance from x is as small as possible.

statement: Each term (x,ei)ei is the projection of x along ei, and the projection s is the sum of the projections of x along each basis element.
quotes: Note that each term $(x, e_{i})e_{i}$ is the projection of x along $e_{i}$
The element s is the sum of the projections of x along each basis element.

statement: Theorem 15.16. If S is a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space V and x is any element of V, then the projection s of x on S is nearer to x than any other element of S: ||x - s|| <= ||x - t|| for all t in S.
quotes: THEOREM 15.16. APPROXIMATION THEOREM. Let S be a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space V, and let x be any element of V.
Then the projection of x on S is nearer to x than any other element of S.

statement: Relative to an orthonormal basis {e1,...,en} of S, the projection of x on S is given by s = sum from i=1 to n of (x,ei) ei.
Let S be a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space V with orthonormal basis {e1,...,en}. For x in V, the element s = sum (x,ei) ei is called the projection of x on the subspace S.
quotes: is called the projection of $x$ on the subspace $S$
Let $S$ be a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space $V$ , and let $\{e_1, \ldots, e_n\}$ be an orthonormal basis for $S$

statement: For any subset S of a Euclidean space V, S-perp is a subspace of V, whether or not S itself is a subspace.
quotes: It is a simple exercise to verify that $S^{\perp}$ is a subspace of V, whether or not S itself is one.

statement: The problem of approximating a given element x of a Euclidean space V by elements of a finite-dimensional subspace S, i.e. finding the element of S that is nearest to x in norm.
quotes: Best approximation of elements in a Euclidean space by elements in a finite-dimensional subspace

statement: For the orthogonal decomposition x = s + s-perp, the norm of x is given by ||x||^2 = ||s||^2 + ||s-perp||^2.
quotes: Moreover, the norm of $x$ is given by the Pythagorean formula

statement: Theorem 15.15: Let V be a Euclidean space and S a finite-dimensional subspace of V. Then every element x in V can be represented uniquely as x = s + s-perp with s in S and s-perp in S-perp, and the norm satisfies the Pythagorean formula.
quotes: THEOREM 15.15. ORTHOGONAL DECOMPOSITION THEOREM. Let V be a Euclidean space and let S be a finite-dimensional subspace of V.
Then every element x in V can be represented uniquely as a sum of two elements, one in S and one in $S^{\perp}$

statement: An element of the (2n+1)-dimensional subspace S spanned by the orthonormal trigonometric functions phi_0, phi_1, ..., phi_{2n}.
quotes: span a subspace $S$ of dimension $2n + 1$ .
The elements of $S$ are called trigonometric polynomials.

statement: The element of the subspace S nearest to x in norm; it equals the projection of x on S, minimizes ||x - t|| over t in S, and is unique (equality holds if and only if t is the projection).
quotes: the equality sign holds if and only if $t = s$ .

statement: The representation of an element x as a sum x = s + s-perp of a component s lying in the subspace S and a component s-perp lying in S-perp, where s-perp = x - s.
quotes: x = s + s ^ {\perp}, \quad \text { where } \quad s \in S \quad \text { and } \quad s ^ {\perp} \in S ^ {\perp}.
s ^ {\perp} = x - s.

statement: Example 1. The projection f_n of a continuous function f on the subspace of trigonometric polynomials; it approximates f better than any other trigonometric polynomial in S, making ||f - f_n|| as small as possible.
quotes: EXAMPLE 1. Approximation of continuous functions on $[0, 2\pi]$ by trigonometric polynomials.
the trigonometric polynomial in (15.22) approximates f better than any other trigonometric polynomial in S, in the sense that the norm $\|f - f_{n}\|$ is as small as possible.

statement: The set of all elements orthogonal to a set S is denoted by S-perp and is called "S perpendicular".
quotes: The set of all elements orthogonal to S is denoted by $S^{\perp}$
